title: Apollo 13
about: An oxygen tank blows three days out, the Moon landing is off, and three astronauts ride a freezing lunar module home while Houston works the problem.
cue: Serve the brisket when Lovell tells Houston they have a problem.

Paprika devilled eggs for July 1969.How to make it8 eggs4 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp white wine vinegar1 tsp sweet paprika1 tbsp chives, snippedLower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water.Peel and halve the eggs and mash the yolks with the mayo, mustard, vinegar and salt.Pipe or spoon back into the whites, dust with paprika and scatter with chives.Square-peg ravioli in a round bowlHouston fits a square filter in a round hole. Ricotta ravioli in hot parmesan broth.How to make it375g fresh square ricotta and spinach ravioli1 L vegetable stock40g parmesan rind or block, plus extra to grate1 garlic clove, sliced1 lemon1 tbsp olive oil1/2 cup basil leavesSimmer the stock with the parmesan and garlic for 10 minutes, then fish out the rind.Drop in the ravioli and cook until they float.Ladle into round bowls, add a squeeze of lemon, oil, basil and grated parmesan.Crew onlyHouston, we have a problem smoked brisketLovell radios Houston with the problem. Texas brisket, pickles and white bread.How to make it1.8kg beef brisket2 tbsp cracked black pepper1 tbsp sea salt flakes2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp garlic powder250ml beef stock8 slices of white bread1 cup dill pickle slices1 white onion, thinly sliced125ml smoky barbecue sauceRub the brisket all over with the pepper, salt, paprika and garlic powder.Sit it fat side up in a roasting tin, pour the stock around, cover tightly with foil and cook at 140°C.Uncover and roast at 200°C until the bark darkens.Rest for 20 minutes, then slice across the grain.Serve with white bread, pickles, onion and barbecue sauce.Aquarius lifeboat chicken pot piesFreezing cold in the lifeboat. Chicken and leek in a golden puff lid.How to make it600g chicken thigh fillets, diced30g butter2 leeks, sliced2 carrots, diced2 tbsp plain flour375ml chicken stock125ml thickened cream1 cup frozen peas2 sheets of frozen puff pastry1 egg, beatenBrown the chicken in the butter, then add the leek and carrot and cook until soft.Stir in the flour, then the stock and cream, and simmer until thick.Stir in the peas, season and spoon into 4 pie dishes.Top with pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.RationedOdyssey heat shield creme bruleeNobody knows if the heat shield held. Vanilla custard under a scorched sugar crust.How to make it600ml pouring cream1 vanilla bean, split6 egg yolks80g caster sugar, plus 4 tbsp for the topsWarm the cream with the vanilla seeds and pod until steaming, then take off the heat.Whisk the yolks and 80g sugar, then whisk in the cream and strain into 4 ramekins.Bake in a water bath at 150°C until just set with a wobble, then chill.Sprinkle each with sugar and scorch with a blowtorch or under a hot grill until dark amber.LoggedLovell's moon night champagneLovell isn't used to the champagne. Brut sparkling with a sugar cube and bitters.How to make it750ml brut sparkling wine4 sugar cubes1 tsp Angostura bitters1 orangeDrop a sugar cube into each of 4 flutes and shake a dash of bitters onto each.Top slowly with the cold sparkling and add a twist of orange peel.Mission Control coffeeOne pot, kept on all night.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
